note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), read offline from the bundled owb-am text, per the founder decision of 2026-11-18 that every Amharic work quotes OWB. This is an Ochorus Original whose English quotes the OWB Balanced edition; the Amharic had used the 1962 UBS wording for the New Testament and Old Testament renderings made in its register. Every quotation was re-quoted to OWB verbatim: each chapter's key-verse block quote, the prayer narratives (Abraham, Jacob, Moses, Hannah, Samuel, David, Solomon, Elijah, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, Jonah, Daniel, Nehemiah, the laments, Habakkuk, Anna and Simeon), the cited verses, the phrases quoted again inside the author's sentences, the chapter titles that quote a verse and the appendices that cite them, and the verses quoted inside Bounds's and Spurgeon's quotations. The book's credit line (about_html and attribution) now credits OWB instead of the 1962 Bible.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse or range, the shortest span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'. Where OWB opens an inner quotation inside a verse, the inner marks are ‹ › (and ‘ ’ one level further in). `self_rendered` rows (each with a `why`) are the reader's own prayers and the author's re-personed summaries that echo a verse.

Judgement calls. Three chapter titles quote their key verse and now take OWB's words, with the appendices following: «አልለቅህም» (Genesis 32:26), «እባክህ፣ ክብርህን ልየው» (Exodus 33:18) and «እግዚአብሔር ሆይ፣ እስከ መቼ ነው?» (Psalm 13:1); chapter 11's title is now «ዓይኖቻችን ግን ወደ አንተ ናቸው» (2 Chronicles 20:12). Psalm 27:4 'one thing' is OWB «አንድ ነገር», so the quoted refrain is «እግዚአብሔርን አንድ ነገር ለመንኩት» and one prose agreement follows it (ምን እንደ ሆነ). The author's own running phrase and chapter 8's title keep «አንዲት ነገር». Exodus 33:19 'goodness' is OWB «በጎነቴ», so the author's 'God's glory is His goodness' became «የእግዚአብሔር ክብር በጎነቱ ነው». 'Stood in the gap' (Psalm 106:23, Ezekiel 22:30) is OWB «በክፍተቱ ቆመ». Chapter 4's title and the author's 'broken place' prose keep «በፍርሱ ቦታ» / «በፈረሰው ስፍራ», as the English does. Jonah 2:2 'Sheol' is OWB «ከሙታን ዓለም ጥልቅ», and the author's word note now reads «በዕብራይስጡ ይህ ‹ሲኦል› ነው». Psalm 51:1 'loyal love … compassion', which the author names as God's character, is OWB «ጽኑ ፍቅር» and «ርኅራኄ» (it was «ቸርነት», «ምሕረት»). Habakkuk 2:4 is OWB «በታማኝነቱ» ('by his faithfulness'), as the English has it, and Paul's quotations of the verse (Romans 1:17) keep OWB's «በእምነት». 1 Thessalonians 5:17 follows the settled «መጸለይን አታቋርጡ» (decision pray-without-ceasing). The refrain 'Not My will, but Yours' is Luke 22:42 «የአንተ ፈቃድ ይሁን እንጂ የእኔ አይሁን» (decision thy-will-be-done). Two citations were corrected to the verse actually quoted: 'Will You destroy the innocent?' is Genesis 18:23 and 'Samuel was displeased … and prayed' is 1 Samuel 8:6.
